objective: Continuation authorized by the owner on 2026-10-28 ('Let's continue with proving L4'), taking the recommendation of CLASS4-PAIRS-20261028-001: prove hypothesis (L4) of its Theorem 7. It serves the complexity program's coprime counting dichotomy (counting homomorphisms from 3-manifold groups into nilpotent-by-cyclic groups N x| C_r, r | p - 1, graded): six class-4 census algebras are #P-hard if (L4) holds, and the twenty other (K)-only algebras need it too. (L4) says that for zero-jump gadget knots whose edge is clean modulo gamma_4, the layer-4 obstruction, affine in the layer-3 data for fixed lower data, has the same linear part as the system assembled from single-edge gadgets and a constant part differing by an element of its image (the indeterminacy of a Massey-type obstruction), so counts are local. Standalone value relative to the nearest known work: Krushkal's additivity of Milnor's mu-bar invariants under band sums modulo indeterminacy applies to links separated by spheres; the gadget's vertex blocks are shared, so no separating sphere exists. Questions: what exactly the junction twists are and where they are absorbed (first on the star K_{1,3}); whether an absorption lemma holds for every edge clean modulo gamma_4 or needs a character condition; a proof of (L4) on all graphs, or a counterexample. Assumptions as before: p >= 5, class at most 4, H1(M; F_p) = 0, bounded sectors, S^3_(d/p)(K) surgeries. No time constraints.
